question.problem: Calculate the point where the ellipse $\frac{(x-2)^{2}}{4}+\frac{(y+6)^{2}}{36}=1$ intercepts the $x$-axis.
question.worked_solution:
To calculate the $x$-intercept, we need to substitute $y=0$ into the equation of the ellipse and solve the resulting equation for $x.$ Doing this, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(x-2)^{2}}{4}+\frac{(y+6)^{2}}{36} & =1 \\ \frac{(x-2)^{2}}{4}+\frac{(0+6)^{2}}{36} & =1 \\ \frac{(x-2)^{2}}{4}+\frac{36}{36} & =1 \\ \frac{(x-2)^{2}}{4}+1 & =1 \\ \frac{(x-2)^{2}}{4} & =0 \\ (x-2)^{2} & =0 \\ x-2 & =0 \\ x & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the ellipse intercepts the $x$-axis at the point $(2,0).$
